title: Identification of condensed coefficient and local-presentation conventions
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with its extending absolute value, and let $X$ be a scheme with Noetherian underlying space. For every finite intermediate field $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Omega$, give $E$ the restricted norm topology and set $E_X=p_X^*C(-,E)$ [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]. Set $\Omega_X=p_X^*\underline\Omega$, where $\underline\Omega(S)$ is the ring of continuous functions on a profinite $S$ with image in one finite intermediate field [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Let $E_X^c$ and $\mathcal C_X^c(E)$ be the coefficient ring and archived bounded constructible category of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]; define $\Omega_X^c$ and $\mathcal C_X^c(\Omega)$ by the identical construction with this specified $\underline\Omega$, as in [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-constructible-serre].

There are canonical ring identifications $E_X=E_X^c$ and $\Omega_X=\Omega_X^c$ induced by the identity on the condensed input and the common point pullback; they preserve units, multiplication, and the maps from coefficient inclusions. Under these identifications the constructibility predicate of [def-sfb-constructible-module] agrees with the archived predicate: there is a finite locally closed stratification such that on a pro-etale cover of each stratum the restricted module is a cokernel $R^m\to R^n\to M\to0$, with $m,n$ finite and $R$ the restricted coefficient ring [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented, def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. This holds for both $E_X$ and $\Omega_X$, using the same stratification and presentations. Thus $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)=\mathcal C_X^c(E)$ and $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Omega)=\mathcal C_X^c(\Omega)$ as full subcategories of their canonically identified ambient ordinary derived categories [def-sfb-dcons-subfield, def-sfb-dcons-qlbar, sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. These identifications preserve all morphisms and bounded cohomology intervals; neither predicate includes finite Tor amplitude or derived completeness.

proof.text: For either coefficient input write $\Lambda=\underline E$ or $\Lambda=\underline\Omega$. For $E$, both conventions take exactly $C(S,E)$ with the restricted norm topology and pointwise ring operations; for $\Omega$, both take exactly the continuous functions whose image lies in a single finite intermediate field. Restrictions in both are precomposition. In [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] and [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category], the site functor is the same $S\mapsto\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{LC}(S,\mathbf Z)$, its inverse image is the same sheafified left Kan extension, and $p_X^*$ is the same composite with $\pi_X^{-1}$. Thus the identity on this input gives the asserted coefficient identification. By [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], both units are $\mathbf Z\cong p_X^*\mathbf Z\to p_X^*\Lambda$, and both multiplications are $p_X^*\Lambda\otimes p_X^*\Lambda\cong p_X^*(\Lambda\otimes\Lambda)\to p_X^*\Lambda$; their identification preserves these maps. A coefficient inclusion acts on sections by $a\mapsto\iota\circ a$ in both conventions, also for the inclusion into the specified finite-subfield-valued $\underline\Omega$. Applying the same functor $p_X^*$ gives the same map, so all coefficient-inclusion squares commute.

proof.text: Use the common coefficient ring $R=\Lambda_X$ from step 1. In [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and the archived convention, an object is the same abelian sheaf $M$ with the same unital associative action $\gamma:R\otimes M\to M$. A morphism is the same sheaf map $f$ satisfying $f\gamma_M=\gamma_N(1_R\otimes f)$. Hence these are the same module category, including identities and composition. For a stratum immersion or a map in a pro-etale covering, both local-presentation definitions use the pulled-back ring and the action obtained by applying the monoidal inverse image to $\gamma$. Therefore the restricted rings, modules and module maps in the two definitions agree, without extending scalars to another coefficient ring.

proof.text: Fix any such restricted ring $R$ and module $M$. By [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module], its finite-presentation witness is $m,n\in\mathbf N$, $f:R^m\to R^n$, and $M\cong\operatorname{coker}(f)$. By [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category] this is precisely the archived local requirement. In the common category of step 2, the regular module is the same $R$ with multiplication as action; its finite sums and the cokernel universal property are the same. Keep $m,n,f$ and the cokernel isomorphism to turn a witness for either convention into a witness for the other. Equivalently, the same quotient map $q:R^n\to M$ has $qf=0$ and the same universal factorization property. This also covers $m=0$ or $n=0$. Keeping the pro-etale cover and each of these witnesses gives both implications for local finite presentation.

proof.text: A witness for [def-sfb-constructible-module] is a finite locally closed stratification $g_a:X_a\to X$, together with a local finite-presentation witness on every stratum. Step 2 identifies the restricted modules, and step 3 keeps each cover and presentation. This gives a witness for the archived constructibility predicate in [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category], and in the reverse direction the same data give the original witness. For $\Omega$ use the identical local-presentation condition specified in [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-constructible-serre]; none of its closure conclusions is needed here. Thus the equivalence holds for both coefficients, with exactly the original strata and presentations.

proof.text: The common module category of step 2 has the same cochain complexes, differentials and chain maps. Its cohomology is computed by the same kernels and images; therefore the quasi-isomorphisms are the same. The ordinary localization construction in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] consequently gives the canonical identification of the ambient derived categories: on complexes and chain maps it is the identity, and it sends the formal inverse of each quasi-isomorphism to the inverse of that same map. These prescriptions in both directions are inverse also on all localized morphisms. The cohomology objects and their vanishing degrees agree. By [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], [def-sfb-dcons-subfield] and [def-sfb-dcons-qlbar], membership is precisely vanishing outside a finite interval and constructibility of every cohomology module. The archived category has precisely these two conditions by [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category], with the specified $\Omega$ input when appropriate. Step 4 equates their constructibility conditions, and the identity on cohomology keeps every possible bound $[a,b]$. Their full subcategories thus identify on all objects and all morphisms. Neither membership condition imposes finite Tor amplitude or derived completeness.

The closure has no cycle and no missing or merged ids, and the item and its deps are not on the route-pivot dropped list. The 5 steps expand old parent O2 steps 1-2 with nothing dropped. Source: main-20261015 lem-sfb-constructible-cocone-obj.proof.md, Modules and Complexes paragraphs; proof correctly marked by agent. Step 1: C(S,E) with the restricted norm is the archived normed-E input by instantiation. For Omega, both sides use the same finite-subfield-valued subsheaf as specified in the Serre node. On the archived side, pi_T^{-1} of def-weil-proetale-inverse-image is the pointwise Lan formula along the same base change as def-sfb-finite-upper-star. Both are left adjoints of the same direct image, so the identification is canonical. Advisory: step 1 says 'the same' where this is a canonical isomorphism. Units, multiplication and the postcomposition inclusion maps agree. Step 2: same internal modules; restriction goes through the monoidal inverse image applied to the action, i.e. mapMod. Step 3: the finite-presentation witness (m, n, f, cokernel iso) carries over, including m=0 or n=0. Step 4: same def-constructible-stratification, covers and presentations; for Omega, only the predicate as written in the Serre node, no closure conclusions. Step 5: the localizations at the same quasi-isomorphisms are identified; same finite-interval bounds, full subcategories, no Tor or completeness condition. Edge cases: X empty, zero module or complex, E=Q_l, and different strata per degree. Duplicate search over nodes citing both the archived and SFB definitions found nothing equivalent. tool_uses are accurate (definitions used by expansion; the Serre node only for its explicit specification).
